reason: Hours by deed: about six for a window up to twenty-two for a killing.
A witness walks to a friend, a phone box or the station; the beat constable acts on what he sees (2.6.1).
Each named person's nerve and loyalty decides how hard he is to pay or frighten; the rule is QUESTIONS 3, already its own part.
Pursuers give up once Tom is unseen 7 s or 70 m (ER-POL-04).

new.name: Police after a deed
new.what: What police do once a deed is reported or a chase lost: a constable at the spot, a search of the streets near it, then back to the beat.
new.design: Once a deed is reported, the beat constable (or a car at manhunt) goes to the spot and stays a while: a body brings tape, a torch at night and Ellis next morning. After a lost chase the pursuer walks the nearby streets for a few game minutes, looking into yards and doorways, and takes the chase up again on sight. The spot is watched ground for the rest of the night: going back there is the risk. Nothing on screen marks where he searches; Tom reads it from the torch, the voice and the parked car.
new.test: After a lost chase the constable searches the nearby streets, resumes on sight, and returns to his beat within the set time; a reported deed always brings an officer to its spot. Check S.

reason: Shaun Hewson's respray and the plate as a mark; a car taken (1.2.10) is a different car to witnesses.
Stand and be searched, run and it is a chase, or a word (A13).
Tom cannot die; beaten, he comes round on the pavement, in Grace Rinaldi's kitchen or in hospital, costing days.
Four stages with signs; armed officers and War-level cars are 2.6.6.

new.name: A street on edge
new.what: Several deeds on one street in a short time make its people jumpier for a while, below the escalation dial.
new.design: Two or three seen deeds on one street within a game day or two set it on edge: doors locked earlier, windows watched longer, witnesses set off to tell sooner, shops shut early, and the constable walks it more often. It eases as the talk cools (2.4.2); the memories stay. Shown in people and doors, never a meter; the dial (2.13) stays the only town-wide step.
new.test: A burst of three seen deeds on one street raises its watchers' readiness to tell and the constable's visits, and both fall back as talk cools; one deed alone does not. Check S.

reason: Back ways, ginnels, yards and bollarded lanes a car cannot follow are part of the Hook's layout as data; roadworks as dressing.
Each deed is its own matter; never taken twice for one.
A weapon in the hand is a give-away; watchers scatter once it is out.
A2: a mark is a doubt (he speeds up or changes route), a face he knows ends the tail: he turns and says so, or runs.
Shops remember; memory is permanent (2.3.1).
People look before they step out (ER-DRIVE-04) and walk round each other; crossings belong in crowd movement.
The week: market day, the Saturday match, Sunday; the crowd and traffic follow the calendar.
Traffic drivers reacting to other cars; a flash of lights at a car on the wrong side is one reaction.
Dusk falls and the lamps come on; lit windows follow routines.
Grip is part of handling; the one wetness value (4.8) lowers it.
Lasting marks on the town: blood on a pavement stays until rain or a bucket washes it, as glass stays broken until mended.
Weather profiles drive the look, the dock water included; smallest budget, no boats beyond scenery (DESIGN 18).
Getting rid of a body; a body in the dock is not gone: canon and DESIGN 7 say a body is never wiped, so it comes up at the basin later and is found.
The fall rule: a fall against a kerb, wall or step after a blow can kill, rarely; there are no heights to fall from (no jumping, the quay edge stops him).
Canon and A11: cars cannot leave the quay into the water; bollards and the edge stop them.
Blood and a limp show condition; blood on him is a give-away (1.4.4).
Fronts: trouble comes back to Tom through the man who runs it (A15).
Greetings by regard include his appearance; dress as a soft key is 2.12.3.
Fronting up: collections and pressure in person; a round is collections repeated (2.17).
Haggling without a meter (A30): the buyer's answers come from his purse and how he regards Tom; access by standing is 2.12.3. No price tables (DESIGN 18).

new.name: Finding an unseen deed
new.what: Who comes upon a deed nobody saw, and when: the owner home to a forced door, a worker at a body, a neighbour at broken glass.
new.design: Every unseen deed leaves its traces (a forced door, glass, a missing thing, a body), and whoever's routine next brings them past finds it: the owner on return, the cleaner at six, the first dock worker. The finder becomes a witness of the aftermath slot only, and reports or tells as a witness would; a body is always found, at latest when the missing man becomes the town's question (2.16). Nothing is found by chance roll: only by routines.
new.test: Every unseen deed with a trace is found by the first person whose routine passes it, and that person holds only the aftermath. Check S: golden rows.

reason: Police after a report: the constable to the spot, then A3 search (A36).
A13: a word talks round a constable with no cause; a note to a bought man; offered to an honest one it is a crime he saw.
A charge joins Ellis's case; she joins the street's crimes to the fire.
Standing is what each person saw and was told, kept for good; never a number (DESIGN 18).
A30: walking away from a haggle is remembered.
A21: a scarf up and a hat down at night break the face rung but are themselves a mark by day.
A21: a second coat breaks the mark rung; a barber changes the look for a week.
The same coat as last night gives him away.
Dress and dirt as soft keys: a filthy man is refused at doors that would open to him clean.
Rita refuses or lowballs goods whose deed is still hot in talk (A30: her answers come from how hot the goods are and how she regards Tom).
Rita's back room opens at rung 2.
Beats fire on states, never on days.
The plan is what casing and tails wrote in the Ledger, chosen in the minute before: which car, who comes, which way in. No planning-board screen; a plan pointed at a person by a sent man is 1.7.2.
Who comes is chosen at dusk; each man's nerve and loyalty is the risk (2.11.2).
Offered by a person, on a state.

new.name: Damage by hand
new.what: Tom himself puts a brick through a window or smashes a car or a shopfront: a message, loud and lasting.
new.design: A job or a pressure can ask Tom to damage something himself: a window, a windscreen, a van's lights, a shop's sign. It is a loud act with the seven slots, heard at the force reach, and the damage stays until mended (2.19). The owner reads it as a message from whoever he suspects; it climbs a rival's ladder if aimed at his. Sending men to do it is the sent verb (1.7.2).
new.test: Every damage act is heard at the force reach, leaves a mark that stays until mended, and is known to its owner by morning. Check S.

reason: A noise or a thrown thing turns a watcher, the beat constable included, or moves him off a door.
Canon: not a driving game; DESIGN 18 cuts a garage of cars; taking a car is A27's single loud act, not a car-theft job family.
Street happenings: each offers a choice with the hands and leaves something the town knows.
A stranger Tom helps can come back later with a favour (A18, the returns-later beat).

new.name: Calling on people
new.what: Time with the people who matter, chosen by Tom: tea at Ada's, the caff with Alison, a walk with Danby; too often and it wears thin.
new.design: Tom can call on a friend or the love interest at a place and hour their routine allows: a short scene of talk, no score and no pass mark. What is said draws on what each knows (the claim check), so a visit after a bad night carries it. Calling again too soon is remembered: a cooler door, a "you again". The friendship that can hold (3.2.5) is built from these visits and the honesty in them.
new.test: A visit is possible only where and when the person's routine allows, shows no score, and a second call inside the set gap draws a cooler answer. Check S.

reason: Rival ladders: each rung said to his face or shown on his street.
Crowd lines by situation: a body or a man down is a situation with its own lines; the crowd's reaction is 2.5.3.

question: Does time with Alison or Danby play as visits Tom chooses, with no score (recommended), or only through story beats?

reason: What rises with him is risk; rivals go after his people.
Side stories run beside the acts from week one.
Each pressure has three answers; the sit-down is accept, defy or counter (3.5.5).
Threaten is rung 3, said in talk or shown.
Bribing the law is the bought constable (A13); paying a witness is 2.5.2.
A man watched stands longer, so alone he gives way sooner.
Leave is always there; scenes skippable (5.8.3).
Honest work is the cab and the fares Tom starts with; the cold-store shift contract explains money (2.15.2).
Windows, not minutes; a missed window ends in a state the town can talk about.
